newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock funds suffer first redemptions of yr.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock funds suffer first redemptions of yr.

text.p: U.S. equity mutual funds suffered their first redemptions of the year for the week ending April 2, according to fund tracking firm AMG Data Services.
Bob Adler, AMG president, said there were net redemptions of $328 million from equity funds for the week.
The last time there were redemptions in stock funds was in December, 1996, he said.
Adler traced the net redemptions to "investors's response to a declining market. It's a graphic example of declining investment sentiment."
Adler said redemptions totalled $1.4 billion in various growth categories, including aggressive and emerging growth.
Growth and income funds and index funds posted cash inflows of $757 million, Adler said.
"Money is still coming into those funds, though at a rate slower than earlier this year," Adler said.
The international fund sector also recorded inflows of $300 million, nearly matching the $342 million for the week of March 26.
